Fact.Name: Net elective payment election amount from Form 3800, Part III, line 6, column (j) (writable)
Fact.Description: Schedule 3 (Form 1040) line 13c, printed "Net elective payment election amount from Form 3800, Part III, line 6, column (j)". IRC 6417(a) treats an applicable entity's election as a payment against the tax imposed by subtitle A equal to the amount of the elected credit, and Schedule 3 Part II carries that payment to Form 1040 line 31. This dictionary does not model Form 3800 Part III columns (h) through (j): nothing here determines an applicable credit, the registration the Secretary requires under IRC 6417(d)(5), or the column (j) net figure, so the filer carries the printed amount across from the Form 3800 they prepared. Nonnegative, because the printed line asks for a payment. Print only until schedule3 /sched3Line14 consumes it. BOUNDARY: the Min $0 limit below is the ONLY constraint on this intake, and the printed rule it does not enforce is a ceiling. "Column (j), Net EPE amount. The net EPE amount is the smaller of: column (h), or column (g) minus column (i). If you have no tax liability figured in Part II, enter the amount from column (h) as the net EPE amount in column (j)" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i3800.pdf, page 10), because "applicable credits must first be applied to tax (if any) before being treated as a payment, amounts treated as a payment (net payment election amounts) are limited to the total of unused credits (without application of any EPE)" (lines 529-532). Nothing in this dictionary derives column (g), (h) or (i), so there is no in-graph quantity to cap this against and the ceiling cannot be enforced where the figure is entered. DIRECTION, and it is the opposite of the other two boundaries in this module: an overstated column (j) flows to Schedule 3 line 13c and Form 1040 line 31 as a refundable payment, so this boundary can OVER-state a payment, where the carryforward and specified-credit boundaries can only under-state a credit. Closing it needs Part III columns (g) through (i) and the applicable-credit determination, which also needs the section 6417(d)(5) registration.

Fact.Name: Form 3800 Part III line 1aa, the filer's own qualified commercial clean vehicle (Form 8936 line 19 as Form 3800 takes it)
Fact.Description: The Schedule A (Form 8936) Part V line 26 credit for the filer's own vehicle, read only when the schedule reaches that line: line 7 answered Yes (a qualified commercial clean vehicle, "Go to Part V"), line 18b answered Yes (subject to the allowance for depreciation) and line 18c answered Yes (acquired for use or to lease to others, not for resale). Line 7 answered No is not a Part V vehicle, so the return carries $0. A No on line 18b or 18c is the printed "Stop here", so the vehicle carries $0. Line 7 is read IsComplete-first, so an unanswered line 7 is not the same answer as a No: a return with no Part V chain (Schedule A line 26 unresolved, or $0) has no vehicle and carries $0, but a return whose Schedule A line 26 resolves above $0 while line 7 is blank is Incomplete, because the routing answer is owed. That is the refusal lines 18b and 18c already get: line 7 Yes with line 18b or 18c unanswered is Incomplete too. When the Form 8936 vehicle collection is Complete and holds at least one copy, this line reads the Schedule A Part V aggregate form8936 /form8936PartVCreditFromScheduleA, the sum of Schedule A line 26 over every copy, and an entered but unattested schedule leaves this line Incomplete because that aggregate withholds. Form 8936 line 19 is printed over "Schedule(s) A", plural, and IRC 45W(a) sums the per vehicle amounts, so a two vehicle return is not one vehicle. That is the arm line 1y already carried. The scalar arms below stay the compatibility path for a return with no copies: one vehicle, as the scalar Schedule A intake models one.

Fact.Name: Is any part of the Form 8936 business credit from a passive activity? (Form 3800 Part III column (d), writable)
Fact.Description: Question: "Is any part of your clean vehicle business credit (Form 8936 line 8 or line 21) from a passive activity, that is, from a trade or business in which you did not materially participate?" Help text: Form 3800 Part III column (d) takes "credits that are subject to the passive activity limitations ... See section 469", and column (e) takes the credit "not subject to the passive activity limitation of section 469 because of your material participation in the trade or business" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i3800.pdf, page 9). Asked when /form3800PartIiiLine1yCredit plus /form3800PartIiiLine1aaCredit is more than $0. Unanswered on that population: both lines' columns (d) and (e) are Incomplete, so Schedule 3 line 6a is owed rather than a silent $0. Yes: the whole amount goes to column (d) and Part I line 2, and Part I line 3 is Incomplete because this dictionary does not model Form 8582-CR, the passive activity credit limitation. No: the whole amount goes to column (e) and Part I line 1. Validation: Yes or No. Feeds the column (d)/(e) facts of lines 1y and 1aa. BOUNDARY: the printed columns split an AMOUNT, not a return. Column (d) takes "your current-year credits that are subject to the passive activity limitations" and column (e) takes "the amount of your current-year credit that is not subject to the passive activity limitation of section 469 because of your material participation" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i3800.pdf, page 9), so a filer who materially participates in one of the two businesses, or in part of one, owes a partial amount in each column. This one all-or-nothing Boolean covers BOTH line 1y (IRC 30D business use) and line 1aa (IRC 45W) together, so a Yes sends every dollar of both lines to column (d): Part I line 1 understates and line 2 overstates the split. DIRECTION and why no filed figure moves: whenever Part I line 2 is above $0, /form3800Line3 refuses (this dictionary does not model Form 8582-CR), so line 6, line 38 and Schedule 3 line 6a are all Incomplete and the return cannot be filed with ANY passive amount, correctly split or not. The approximation is therefore confined to a population that is already blocked, and it cannot over-claim. Witnessed by tests/nodes/ty2025/form3800/form3800-passive-8936-credit-refused-at-part-i-line3 (Yes, the whole $7,500 in column (d), Part I line 1 $0, line 3 Incomplete, Schedule 3 line 6a Incomplete) and form3800-passive-question-unanswered-incomplete. Closing it needs a per-line passive AMOUNT intake, one Dollar writable for line 1y and one for line 1aa, read only on a Yes, with column (d) the entered portion and column (e) the line minus it - a new interview obligation for the application, so it is not folded into this Description.

Fact.Name: Section 6418(g)(3) reaches this statement's credit, so Schedule A (Form 3800) line 12 is "applicable"
Fact.Description: True only when line 1 is answered with one of the three Form 3468 boxes: Part III (the section 48C qualifying advanced energy project credit), Part V (the section 48E clean electricity investment credit) or Part VI (the section 48 energy credit). Those are the three eligible credits of IRC 6418(f)(1)(A)(ix) through (xi), and IRC 6418(g)(3) reaches "any portion of an eligible credit described in clauses (ix) through (xi)" and no other. Every other box on line 1 is a production or fuel credit, not investment credit property, so no basis reduction and no recapture notification can arise and the printed "(if applicable)" on line 12 is not satisfied. False when line 1 names any other box, and ALSO false while line 1 is unanswered: in that state the module does not claim to know, and the consumers below keep requiring the line 12 answer, which is the conservative reading of an unanswered routing box.

Fact.Name: This Schedule A (Form 3800) has a No on a certification line or on the signatures
Fact.Description: True when any of lines 7, 8, 9 and 10, or the line 13a/13b signature answer, is answered No, and also when line 12 is answered No on a statement whose line 1 box makes section 6418(g)(3) applicable. False while every answered one is Yes, including when some are unanswered. Line 12 is read through ../recaptureNotificationApplies, because both the form and the instructions qualify line 12 with "(if applicable)" and section 6418(g)(3) reaches only the section 48, 48C and 48E credits. A No on line 12 against, say, a section 45X production credit on the Form 7207 box is the correct answer to an inapplicable question, and used to drop the whole transferred credit to $0.

Fact.Name: The credit this Schedule A (Form 3800) transfers to the filer (Part III column (f), positive)
Fact.Description: Line 3 when every certification and the signature answer is Yes; $0 when any is No; Incomplete while none is No and any is unanswered, or while line 3 is unanswered. The line 12 answer is required only when it is applicable. The arm below asks for it unless line 1 IS answered and ../recaptureNotificationApplies is false, that is unless the statement's box is known not to be one of the three Form 3468 boxes section 6418(g)(3) reaches. An unanswered line 1 still requires line 12, so a statement that says nothing about its own credit is not let through. The amount is the LESSER of line 3 and line 5, and Incomplete while line 5 is blank: the instructions say "Complete Schedule A (Form 3800) in its entirety", and item B(ii) and the schedule's own presence gate (form3800a /form3800aStatementAnswered) count a statement only once lines 3 and 5 are both answered, so a blank line 5 must not put a credit in column (f) that no attached statement supports. IRC 6418(a) permits a transfer of "all (or any portion specified in the election) of an eligible credit determined with respect to such taxpayer", so nothing above the credit the transferor determined, which is what line 5 states, is an eligible transferred credit. The cap states the ALLOWABLE amount; the IRC 6418(g)(2) addition to tax on the excess, which is that amount plus 20 percent, is a separate unmodelled thing. The statement contributes $0 to THIS return when it names another year. IRC 6418(d) puts the credit in "the first taxable year of the transferee taxpayer ending with, or after, the taxable year of the eligible taxpayer with respect to which the credit was determined", so for a calendar-year 2025 return the transferor's year (Schedule A line 6) must itself end inside 2025: a line 6 in 2024 or earlier was taken into account in an earlier transferee year, and one in 2026 or later belongs to a later one. Schedule A line 11, where the filer states the first transferee year, is read the same way. Both are read only when ANSWERED, so the many statements that leave the dates blank are unchanged - the module does not start demanding a date it never asked for.

Fact.Name: Form 3800 Part V column (a) for this statement: the Part III line number of the transferred credit
Fact.Description:
Part V column (a) is the Part III line number of the credit this transfer election statement carries, and the instructions say to take it from Part III itself. The Schedule A line 1 box names the form (and, where the form has more than one, the part) the transferor completed, and the Form 3800 instructions print the transferable credits with their section, form and part, which fixes eleven of the twelve boxes on a single Part III row: Form 3468 Part III to 1d, Form 3468 Part V to 1v, Form 3468 Part VI to 4a, Form 7207 to 1b, Form 8933 to 1x, Form 7210 to 1g, Form 7211 to 1gg, Form 7213 to 1u, Form 7218 to 1q, Schedule A (Form 8911) Part II to 1s, and Form 8864 to 1l. The Form 8864 assignment is the diesel row rather than the sustainable aviation fuel row 1ff because the instruction names section 40A, the small agri-biodiesel producer credit; section 40B is the aviation fuel one and is not in the list. The Form 7213 assignment is Part II, row 1u, rather than the Part I row 1cc, because the instruction names section 45U and Part II.
THE TWELFTH BOX IS UNDECIDABLE AND THIS FACT SAYS SO BY GOING INCOMPLETE. Form 8835 is printed on Part III twice under the same caption, row 1f and row 4e, and the two differ only by whether the section 45 credit is a specified credit in the facility's first four years - a fact about the facility that nothing on Schedule A (Form 3800) asks and nothing in this dictionary holds. No catch-all arm follows the eleven, so an answered Form 8835 box and an unanswered box alike run off the end of the Switch and resolve Incomplete, which prints the column (a) cell BLANK. That is the safe direction: a blank cell on a form the filer must review is a visible gap, while a guessed row letter would place a credit on a line whose limitation regime is not the one the law gives it.
The Schedule A box for the section 30C credit is printed "Schedule A (Form 8911), Part II" while the instruction list and the Part III row both read "Form 8911, Part I". Row 1s is the only Form 8911 row Part III prints, so the assignment does not turn on which of the two captions is the current one.

Fact.Name: This statement's Form 3800 Part V column (c)(2) transferor identifying number

Unlike the header chooser (form3800a ../form3800aTransferorIdentifyingNumber), it has no empty-string fallback: with neither number answered it is Incomplete, so a Part V row that does not exist, or a statement with no number, prints blank rather than a placeholder. Fact.Name: Form 3800 Part III column (f), the credits transferred to the filer
Fact.Description: The sum of every statement's /creditTransferredIn: the positive column (f) amount a transferee enters (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i3800.pdf, page 9). $0 when the filer holds no statement. Summed over all boxes rather than placed on each credit's own Part III line. For an individual transferee the whole amount is taken as passive and reaches Part I line 2: "You are a noncorporate taxpayer ... to which was transferred an IRA 2022 credit ... Then you must apply the rules under sections 38 and 469. File Form 8582-CR" (lines 557-566). BOUNDARY: summing over all boxes is not only a placement simplification, it can put a SPECIFIED credit on the wrong line. Two of the twelve line 1 boxes name credits IRC 38(c)(4)(B) lists as specified - Form 3468 Part VI, the section 48 energy credit, through clause (x) (the section 46 credit attributable to the section 48 energy credit), and Form 8835, the section 45 credit in a facility's first four years, through clause (iv) (26 U.S.C. 38, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-2024-title26-section38&num=0&edition=2024). Form 3800 prints those on Part III line 4a and line 4e (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f3800.pdf, page 4), from where they reach Part II Section C, and the instructions say plainly "Do not include specified credits on line 3" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i3800.pdf, page 6). This dictionary has no Part III line 4 and no Section C, so such a credit is summed here instead, and it would be held to the Section A limit. DIRECTION: that limit is the harsher one, so the transferee would be UNDER-allowed and over-charged; it never over-claims. No dollar is wrong TODAY only because /form3800Line3 is Incomplete for every transferee return, which is a blocked return rather than a wrong one. Whoever builds the Form 8582-CR module must build Part III line 4 and Section C with it, or the first returns it unblocks will be under-allowed. Same build as the specified-credit boundary at /form3800Line38.

Fact.Name: This return must use Form 3800 Part V
Fact.Description:
Part V breaks a Part III line down when more than one facility, pass-through entity or transferor feeds that ONE line. The printed Part III caption states the trigger - more than one number applicable for column (b) or (c) for a Part III line - and the instructions state it again for a transferee: complete Part V when there are multiple facilities from which one of the eligible credits was received, and do not need to use Part V when there is only one facility or one pass-through entity for that credit.
MEASURED PER CREDIT BOX, WHICH IS PER PART III LINE. This fact is true when two or more ANSWERED transfer election statements name the SAME Schedule A line 1 box. Each Schedule A carries one transferor and one registration number, so two statements on one box are two numbers on one Part III line, which is the printed trigger. The twelve boxes map one-to-one onto twelve distinct Part III rows, so counting by box is counting by line; the Form 8835 box is counted like the rest even though its own row letter is undecidable, because two Form 8835 statements are two numbers on whichever of rows 1f and 4e the credit belongs to.
FALSE, NOT INCOMPLETE, ON EVERY RETURN THAT HOLDS NO STATEMENT. The first arm answers an unanswered collection directly, so an ordinary return reads Complete false rather than the Placeholder a bare filtered count would hand back.
TWO DECLARED LIMITS, both in the direction of NOT printing Part V. A statement whose line 1 box is unanswered joins no count, so a return holding two such statements does not trigger Part V here. And the multiple-pass-through-entity and multiple-facility-per-statement cases are not modelled at all: this dictionary holds no facility and no pass-through entity, only the statement, so one statement covering two facilities of one credit is invisible. Both under-trigger. Under-triggering leaves the aggregate on Part III and prints no breakdown, which is the state the form is in today; over-triggering would print a breakdown table the dictionary cannot fill.

Fact.Name: This partnership or S corporation Schedule K-1 reports a credit this dictionary does not compute

Codes that do NOT trip: O (backup withholding, which the instructions send to Form 1040 line 25c), H (undistributed capital gains credit, sent to Schedule 3 line 13a) and AP through AU (tax credit bond credits, sent to Form 8912) pass because they are not Form 3800 Part III credits, not because this dictionary carries them: only code O is read today, and a code H or AP through AU amount is outside this guard; AY and AZ are the Form 8936 credits this dictionary computes, and they do not trip while the matching pass-through intake carries an amount (/form3800K1CodeAyCarriedByForm8936, /form3800K1CodeAzCarriedByForm8936). An answered amount with no code trips (the credit cannot be placed); a code with no amount, or an amount of $0, does not. A negative amount trips. Every read is IsComplete-fenced, so an untouched row is Complete false.

Complete on every row, because the code and amount tests open on IsComplete, so the reader over the row table is Complete once the table is answered.

Fact.Name: Some partnership or S corporation Schedule K-1 reports a credit this dictionary does not compute
Fact.Description: True when at least one item of scheduleE /formK1s has /formK1s/*/form3800CreditSlotNotComputed true. The count sits inside an IsComplete Switch on the collection, defaulting to false, so a return that never opened the K-1 section is Complete false, not Placeholder.

Fact.Name: This estate or trust Schedule K-1 reports a credit this dictionary does not compute
Fact.Description: True when at least one of the box 13 rows on THIS Schedule K-1 (Form 1041) has an answered amount other than $0 and a code other than A (credit for estimated taxes, Form 1040 line 26), B (backup withholding, Form 1040 line 25c) or P (credit to holders of tax credit bonds, a Form 8912 credit and not a Form 3800 one). The other codes the form prints (C through O, Q, S, T and ZZ other credits) are general business credit components, and R is credit recapture; none reaches a computed line. An unknown code trips too; an answered amount with no code trips; a code with no amount, or $0, does not. Every read is IsComplete-fenced.

Fact.Description: One row of /form1041K1s/*/creditEntries as /form1041K1s/*/form3800CreditSlotNotComputed reads it: True when this row passes the test /form1041K1s/*/form3800CreditSlotNotComputed applies to every row (code A or B or P); otherwise False. Complete on every row, because the code and amount tests open on IsComplete, so the reader over the row table is Complete once the table is answered.

Fact.Name: Some estate or trust Schedule K-1 reports a credit this dictionary does not compute
Fact.Description: True when at least one item of scheduleE /form1041K1s has /form1041K1s/*/form3800CreditSlotNotComputed true. IsComplete Switch on the collection defaulting to false, so an absent collection is Complete false.

Fact.Name: A Form 1099-PATR box 12 pass-through credit is carried by Form 8941 line 15
Fact.Description: True when form8941 /form8941Line15PassThroughCredit is more than $0. Form 8941 line 15's own help text names "Form 1099-PATR box 12 (or another notice of credit allocation) when it is this credit" as one of the sources it stands in for, so a filer who has already entered the pass-through small employer health insurance premium credit there has carried the credit to Form 3800 Part III line 4h; the box 12 arm of /form1099Patrs/*/form3800CreditComponentNotComputed does not also refuse it for the same dollar. This is a return-level release, not a per-item one: the fact graph has no link from a specific Form 1099-PATR item's box 12 to the Form 8941 line 15 total, so any answered box 12 amount is released once Form 8941 line 15 carries any pass-through credit at all. Always Complete: form8941 /form8941Line15PassThroughCredit is complete-safe (unanswered reads $0).

Fact.Name: This Form 1099-PATR reports a general business credit component this dictionary does not compute
Fact.Description: True when this Form 1099-PATR item carries an answered box 10 (investment credit), box 11 (work opportunity credit) or box 12 (other credits and deductions) amount other than $0 that this dictionary does not carry to a computed Form 3800 Part III line. Box 10 and box 11 always trip: this dictionary builds neither Form 3468 (the investment credit form box 10 names) nor Form 5884 (the work opportunity credit form box 11 names). Box 12 trips UNLESS /form3800PatrBox12CreditCarriedByForm8941 is true: the box 12 instructions send the filer to "the instructions for the specific credit form", and Form 8941's own line 15 help text names Form 1099-PATR box 12 as one of its sources, so a filer who reported the credit there is not refused a second time for it. A negative amount trips, the same convention /form3800K1CreditNotComputed and /form3800EstateTrustK1CreditNotComputed use for a K-1 credit slot. Every read is IsComplete-fenced, so an untouched box does not trip.

Fact.Name: Some Form 1099-PATR reports a general business credit component this dictionary does not compute
Fact.Description: True when at least one item of scheduleF /form1099Patrs has /form1099Patrs/*/form3800CreditComponentNotComputed true. IsComplete Switch on the collection defaulting to false, so an absent collection is Complete false; the same shape /form3800EstateTrustK1CreditNotComputed uses.

Fact.Name: Knockout: the return carries a general business credit component this dictionary does not compute
Fact.Description: Blocks submission when the return carries a Form 3800 Part III credit that this dictionary does not figure from its own component form. Form 3800 Part III computes lines 1j, 1dd and 1ee (Form 8881), 1s (Form 8911), 1y and 1aa (Form 8936) and 4h (Form 8941); every other component form is not built, and a return that files with such a credit either drops it or takes a figure nothing here checked against its form. Four arms, each Complete-safe. (1) schedule3 /writableSchedule3Line6aGeneralBusinessCredit answered and not $0: the attested other-credit total that lands on line 1zz; the intake still feeds line 1zz, but the return is refused. (2) /form3800K1CreditNotComputed: a partnership or S corporation Schedule K-1 credit slot with a code this dictionary does not carry. (3) /form3800EstateTrustK1CreditNotComputed: the same for an estate or trust Schedule K-1 box 13. (4) /form1099PatrCreditComponentNotComputed: a Form 1099-PATR item with an answered box 10 (investment credit, Form 3468), box 11 (work opportunity credit, Form 5884) or box 12 (other credits and deductions, released only when Form 8941 line 15 already carries a pass-through credit) amount other than $0 (FED-3800-PATR-CREDITS-UNREAD). NOT members: the Form 8881 credits on lines 1j, 1dd and 1ee, the Form 8911 credit on line 1s, the Form 8936 credits and the Form 8941 credit on line 4h (computed), the Schedule A (Form 3800) transferee credits and a passive Form 8936 credit (both already Incomplete at /form3800Line3, which refuses them), and the net elective payment intake /writableForm3800PartIiiLine6ColumnJNetElectivePaymentElection, a payment line rather than a Part III credit. RESIDUE: the code AY and AZ release is return-level, not per K-1, so two K-1s both carrying code AY pass once the pass-through intake carries any amount, even one K-1's share. A filer who holds a component credit and enters it nowhere is not refused, because nothing in the graph knows it exists; a carryforward to 2025 has no intake at all. A Form 1099-PATR box 12 amount that is a DEDUCTION rather than a credit is refused anyway, because the printed box has no field split between the two.

Fact.Name: The return carries a Form 3800 Part III line 6 column (j) net elective payment amount
Fact.Description: True when /writableForm3800PartIiiLine6ColumnJNetElectivePaymentElection is answered and more than $0. Part III columns (g) through (j) for an elective payment election (the gross amount, the part applied against tax and the net amount) and the section 6417(d)(5) registration number are not figured here, so the printed Form 3800 cannot be completed for this return. Always Complete.

Fact.Name: The return carries a general business credit subject to the passive activity limits
Fact.Description: True when Part I line 2 or Part II line 32 is known and more than $0, or the filer answers Yes to a passive credit carryforward (/writableForm3800HasPassiveCreditCarryforward): the passive current-year credits of Part III column (d), every Schedule A (Form 3800) transferee credit in column (f), and the passive carryforwards of Part IV column (d). The amount allowed needs Form 8582-CR (Part I line 3, Part II line 33, Part III column (g)), which this dictionary does not model. Always Complete.

Fact.Name: The return holds an answered Schedule A (Form 3800) transfer election statement
Fact.Description: True when at least one answered transfer election statement is on the return. The transferee path prints Part III column (f), item B, Part V and Schedule A (Form 3800); Part V columns (d)(4), (g) and (h) through (k) are not figured here, and the credit transferred in is passive and meets Form 8582-CR. Read IsComplete-first, so an untouched return is Complete false.

Fact.Name: The return carries a non-passive general business credit carryforward to 2025
Fact.Description: True when Part I line 4 or Part II line 34 is more than $0. Part IV (each credit's row, the originating tax year in column (b), and columns (g) through (i), the part applied against tax in the IRC 38(d) order and the carryforward to 2026) is not built, so the printed Form 3800 cannot be completed for this return. Always Complete.

Fact.Name: The return carries a pass-through general business credit whose Part III column (c) EIN you have not entered
Fact.Description: True when a credit passed through from a partnership or S corporation (or, for Form 8941 line 15, a cooperative, estate or trust) reaches a Part III line more than $0 -- Form 8881 line 7, 10 or 14, Form 8941 line 15, or Form 8911 line 2 -- and the filer has not entered that entity's EIN for column (c). Column (c) takes "that pass-through entity's employer identification number" for a credit allocated from a pass-through entity. Answering the EIN releases this arm for that leg; leaving a positive pass-through amount unanswered here does not. (The Form 8936 pass-through credits on lines 1y and 1aa have their EIN questions already.) Always Complete.

Fact.Name: Knockout: this return must attach a Form 3800 that cannot be completed here
Fact.Description: This return must attach Form 3800, and one of its parts cannot be completed here yet: a net elective payment amount (Part III columns (g) through (j)), a general business credit from a passive activity or a credit transferred to you under section 6418 (Form 8582-CR and Part V), a Schedule A (Form 3800) transfer election statement, a general business credit carried forward from an earlier year (Part IV), or a credit passed through to you by a partnership, S corporation, cooperative, estate or trust whose employer identification number you have not entered for Part III column (c). This return cannot be filed here. True when any of /form3800NetElectivePaymentEntered, /form3800PassiveCreditEntered, /form3800TransferStatementEntered, /form3800CarryforwardEntered or /form3800PassThroughCreditWithoutEin is true; each is IsComplete-fenced, so an untouched return is false. A return whose only credits are the current-year, non-passive credits this dictionary computes (Part III lines 1j, 1s, 1y, 1aa, 1dd, 1ee and 4h) prints Form 3800 through the IRS3800 render gate and is not refused here; a pass-through share of those credits with its column (c) EIN entered is not refused either.
